title: Recertification Due Date on Long-Term Hardship Holds
content:
For Hardship and Protective Holds, the updated physician's medical or disability certification asked for before a status review of a running Long-Term Hardship Hold has a due date defined as follows.

## Clause

The recertification is due on the last day of the upcoming status review's overdue window: the days allowed for the recertification run from the day of the request to the due date of the status review that next falls due, reviews falling due every review interval counted from the hold's start date, plus the tier's review overdue days. For the recertification, a status review falling due on the day of the request counts as already fallen due, so the review the recertification is for is the following one. The recertification due date never falls after the hold's current end date. The days allowed for the recertification are a whole number of calendar days and are not rounded.

## As condition and result

| Step of the definition | Content |
|---|---|
| Review the recertification is for | The next review to fall due after the day of the request (a review due that very day counts as already fallen due) |
| Last day of its overdue window | That review's due date plus the tier's review overdue days |
| Days allowed | Calendar days from the request to that last day |
| Limit | The due date is never after the hold's current end date; where it would be, the due date is the current end date |

The review interval and the review overdue days are the Long-Term Hardship Hold's figures in the product's status review calendar.

## Worked examples (hypothetical; interval 60 days and overdue days 15, as the calendar sets for this tier)

A hold started on 1 March; reviews fall due on 30 April, 29 June and 28 August.

- **Request on 20 June, current end date 27 August.** The next review is 29 June, 9 days away. Days allowed: 9 plus 15, that is 24; due date 14 July.
- **Request on 20 June, current end date 5 July.** The count of 24 would reach 14 July, after the current end date, so the due date is 5 July and the days allowed are 15.
